transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we dive in, let me set the frame for today's enforcement-review meeting. As you all know, Northstar Systems' quarterly royalty reports have shown inconsistent usage figures, and the commercial team wants this addressed without disrupting the existing license. Our agreement does permit a royalty audit when reporting discrepancies are identified. However, I will not approve any formal notice or demand to Northstar until I've heard from each of you -- finance, IP, privacy, and account counsel -- on your respective areas of concern. So let's work through this systematically. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'd like to start by sharing what my reconciliation has found. I compared Northstar's usage ledger against their royalty reports and confirmed an underpayment of exactly $284,600 for the third and fourth quarters of 2025. This reconciliation is still awaiting controller sign-off and has not yet been entered in the legal enforcement dashboard, so I want everyone to be aware that the figure is preliminary until that sign-off is complete.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I completed a clause review of the license agreement yesterday and need to share the audit notice requirements with the group. The agreement specifies that an audit notice must be sent at least 10 business days before the audit, must identify the auditor as Grant & Pike LLP, and may not be replaced by a general breach letter. I haven't circulated these requirements until now, but they're critical for shaping whatever enforcement approach we take.

transcript.text: I need to share what I've confirmed on the privacy side. I spoke with Northstar's privacy lead, and the audit materials will include EU employee-level usage records. The approved method is an on-site review using pseudonymized records, with no export of EU employee data -- rather than a remote transfer of the raw files. This is critical because any audit plan we put forward needs to respect this constraint. We cannot simply request that Northstar transfer raw usage files to us or to Grant & Pike remotely; the review must be conducted on-site with pseudonymized data.

transcript.text: I need to share something important from this week's executive-account call that hasn't made it into the enforcement draft yet. I learned that Northstar will accept a private cure process only if two conditions are met: first, they receive 30 days to cure after the demand is sent, and second, the company makes no public accusation. This commercial condition is not currently reflected in the enforcement draft, and I think it's critical that we factor it into our plan before Elena makes a final decision.

commitments.detail: Send formal audit notice at least 10 business days before the audit, identifying Grant & Pike LLP as the named auditor, per the license agreement requirements.
Conduct audit via on-site review of pseudonymized EU employee-level usage records with no remote transfer or export of raw EU employee data.
Provide 30 days to cure after the demand is sent, with no public accusation, per Northstar's commercial conditions for a private cure process.
Demand $284,600 for confirmed underpayment in Q3 and Q4 2025, contingent on controller sign-off of the reconciliation.
